snippet.title: FE: Bases and Bandits, Full LTC Playthrough [Romhack]
snippet.description:
Chapters 1-5 are completed in 3, 5, 4, 4, and 6 turns respectively for a total of 22 turns.

Well hello there! In less than 12 hours I went ahead and posted a full-length LTC playthrough too. I first figured out the 6-turn clear of Ch5 during some downtime at work yesterday, and went to record it today, then I began working through Ch3 and 4 to figure out a low-turn clear for those, initially coming up with a 5-turn clear and a shoddy proof-of-concept 10-turn clear respectively, going back to Ch3 to find a 4-turn soon after and then solidify a 7-turn for Ch4. I recorded a full playthrough that beat the game in 25 turns but something didn't feel right. Ch4 had optimizations to be made, and then I saw it very obviously, "why am I not flying over the cliffs as soon as possible?" so I went and found a 5-turn clear. Satisfied with a total count of 23 turns, I went ahead and recorded that too, but I shortly realized I could possibly squeeze yet another turn out of Ch4! So I had to go back and prove it and then record the entire run again for a total turn count of 22. My goodness! The 7-turn clear is pretty neat and makes these razor-thin level-up margins safer, but I got them all the same. Ch5 however has been modified since my last video for a version that fits both the 23 or 22 turn playthrough, thankfully! I wouldn't know what to do if someone couldn't plug the wall on the very final turn like Roshea could with that final level-up.

Funnily enough, on my first replay of the hack, I had used Messenger as my high-movement training project, and she may yet work for that role if her 2nd level also gives her a defense point (I don't recall if it does), but it shouldn't be able to save any more turns. What do I tell you man, high movement is really good, finding a way to make your high movement units good is always worthwhile. I have a bit of a reputation (among anyone who has had me playtest their hack) in utilizing the full utility and combat potential of earlygame fliers and Jagens while simultaneously discarding that "really good" armor knight. I can't help it, it makes the game so much fun.

I'd like to thank ArcherBias for making this wonderful romhack. It is entirely deterministic: you will always hit, you will always crit if you're using the killing edge, your level-ups will always be the same, so on and so forth. It is very fun and rewarding and I came back to it after years of remembering it fondly. Giving this romhack an LTC is the best I can give it in return. Check it out sometime and pick some ideas from it, it's on FEU!
